findings.explanation: res.render supports either (view, options, callback) or (view, callback); a function in the second position wins and resets options. It writes res.locals into opts._locals, overwriting any caller-supplied _locals and mutating an object supplied as options. app.render then merges those locals. A supplied truthy callback is passed through and suppresses automatic response/error handling. Otherwise the default callback sends successful output with res.send and forwards callback-delivered errors to req.next. There is no callback type guard: a truthy non-function is accepted here and can fail downstream.

The spread order gives app.locals lowest precedence, response/_locals next, and explicit option properties highest; opts._locals itself also remains an option because opts is spread last. cache equal to null or undefined is not an explicit override and falls back to the app's view-cache setting. Explicit false (or another falsy value) disables View-cache lookup/insertion, while truthy enables it. A fresh app enables view cache by default only in production; otherwise it remains disabled unless configured. The View cache is keyed solely by the requested name. A hit reuses the existing View and skips the current View constructor, roots, engine selection, and lookup. On a miss, only a View with a truthy path is cached, and insertion occurs before tryRender, so a later render error does not evict it. The separate app.engines registry is reused independently of this flag; renderOptions.cache is merely passed to the selected engine, whose own caching behavior is not established by Express.

The built-in View first uses path.extname(name). An existing filename extension selects that extension's engine and does not require a default engine. Without an extension, the configured default engine is required, normalized to have a leading dot, and appended to the lookup filename. Express sets no default view engine, so an extensionless name throws unless one was configured. A truthy engine-registry entry is reused without another View-side type check. app.engine normally normalizes the extension and rejects non-functions, but direct registry mutation is not covered by that guard. If no entry exists, View requires the extension name without its dot, reads __express, requires it to be a function, and caches it only after validation. Missing-module/initialization errors and the explicit invalid-__express error escape the constructor. The app's default configurable View is this implementation, but app.set('view', ...) can replace it, so these selection rules are not guaranteed for a custom constructor.

Built-in lookup converts root to an array and examines roots in their configured order, stopping at the first successful path. Within each root it first tests the resolved direct filename, then <name-without-extension>/index<extension>; both candidates must stat successfully and be regular files. A directory or other non-file therefore falls through. tryStat catches every synchronous stat error and returns undefined, treating absence, permissions, and other stat failures as misses rather than throwing. If both candidates miss, lookup continues to the next root; after all roots fail, resolve/lookup returns undefined. The default root is path.resolve('views'), but views is configurable. These filesystem rules belong to the built-in View and need not hold for a custom app view.

A completed View construction with no path follows a different path: app.render creates a Failed to lookup view error, attaches the View as err.view, and immediately calls done(err), without caching or rendering. That delivery is synchronous at this source level. In contrast, new View(...) occurs before tryRender and has no surrounding catch, so missing/default-engine errors, require failures, invalid __express, custom-constructor throws, and other constructor exceptions propagate instead of being callback-delivered. tryRender catches only exceptions thrown synchronously while calling view.render and converts them to callback(err); exceptions thrown later by asynchronous engine work are outside this stack. With res.render's default callback, callback-delivered errors go to req.next; an explicit callback receives them instead. Constructor throws bypass that default callback. Direct app.render also provides no default callback of its own.

The built-in View calls the selected engine with path, options, and an onRender callback. If the engine invokes onRender before returning, View copies the exact arguments and callback-call context and delivers them on process.nextTick, so the final callback is not synchronous. After the engine returns, later engine callbacks are forwarded immediately in their own asynchronous turn with callback.apply(this, arguments), again preserving context and arguments. No once/done guard exists. Multiple engine callback invocations produce multiple final callback invocations. A synchronous callback followed by a synchronous engine throw can also schedule one delivery and then cause tryRender to deliver the thrown error, yielding two calls. Thus neither the built-in path nor configurable custom View/engine code guarantees at-most-once callback delivery; Express also cannot prove whether an arbitrary engine calls back, calls once, or throws asynchronously.
